translation.title: Indomethacin Cream
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and reduction of inflammation in degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, humeral epicondylitis (such as tennis elbow), muscle pain, and swelling and pain after injury.
translation.usage: Depending on your symptoms, apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times a day and rub it in gently so that it is absorbed well.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you have experienced hypersensitivity reactions (asthma, a history of bronchospasm, rhinitis or angioedema) caused by aspirin or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, or for children under 14. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if you are breastfeeding, or for children. Do not use it on skin with lesions (bleeding skin disorders, eczema, infected lesions, burns or wounds), or in the eyes or on mucous membranes. This medicine is for external use only. Do not use an occlusive (airtight) dressing over it. Adverse reactions may occur - occasionally itching, redness, rash, contact dermatitis and eczema, and rarely a feeling of heat, swelling, flushing, anaphylaxis, photosensitivity, a burning sensation, irritation, dryness and tingling, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness; if any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Hypersensitivity reactions (skin reactions, bronchospasm, a drop in blood pressure leading to shock) and, in special cases, aseptic meningitis (headache, nausea, vomiting, fever, stiffness at the back of the neck or clouded consciousness) can occur. In patients with psoriasis, symptoms may worsen.
